gate_bindings.accepted: The complete uniform SU(2) bulk dictionary gives r=4/g^4, tau=96/g^4 and local norm 672/g^4. The actual selected bridge requires g^4>=32; the frozen a_n=a0/n, g_n^2=1/n path violates this sufficient condition for every n>=1. Finite whole-star and all-contained-plaquette boundaries differ.
limitations: This is failure of a specified sufficient certificate, not a no-gap or continuum-impossibility theorem.
The positive source constants c1(S), c2(S) remain unevaluated.
Bulk interaction equality does not identify different boundary-state limits; common energy and actual ground centering must be retained.
General weak-coupling obstruction is inherited from R18-B2; the full I1 dictionary, bridge cap and boundary audit are the incremental result. Scientific priority unverified.

gate_bindings.accepted: Common positive energy multiplication and scalar shifts preserve all sufficient-membership ratios. With electric alpha fixed, a nonnegative common magnetic multiplier s belongs to the inherited coefficient domain exactly when s<=g^4/32, s<c1*g^4/672 and s<g^4/(1344*c2). Therefore along g->0 any such s tends to zero.
limitations: The iff concerns the inherited sufficient domain, not necessary conditions for an actual gap.
The s=0 case is a separate decoupled electric control, not a nonzero magnetic bridge.
Common energy multiplication changes physical gaps and requires reciprocal time rescaling; E_star and hbar remain fixed.
The c1,c2 constants are unevaluated. Independent magnetic suppression changes the action and does not prove physical equivalence or a continuum limit. Scientific priority unverified.

gate_bindings.accepted: The source-specific audit constructs a nonzero physical Wilson excitation within one complete 24-link factor and proves the grouped site budget J=28|tau|. Gauvin's four-active-fine-link argument, Haar vacuum and at-most-three-site support do not transfer unchanged to the actual selected-strip reference and four-site grouping. The numerical I1 radius remains insufficient in this investigation.
limitations: The one-factor witness rejects an incorrect coarse-factor inference, not the external source's actual fine-link statement or its numerical energy bound.
The qualitative I1 theorem and I2 missing-constant ledger remain inherited; no convenient c1 or c2 has been inserted.
This audit does not prove that explicit constants cannot be derived, that the actual gap fails, or that the external paper is false.
Scientific priority is unverified and no continuum construction follows.

gate_bindings.accepted: For every nonempty finite I1 complete-factor volume with the actual selected-strip reference and full whole-star omitted interaction, both signs of |tau|<=1/100000000 admit a unique ground and a physical gap at least alpha/16. The proof derives the four-site creation majorant G(t)=16 exp(8t)(1+10t), full scalar fixed point, centered excited-sector exclusion and removal of onsite representation cutoffs. The forward full-Hilbert-space strengthening is separately proved and reviewed.
limitations: This is a deliberately conservative finite-volume theorem uniform over the declared volumes, not an infinite-volume state-identification theorem.
The proof does not evaluate Yarotsky's named c1/c2 or HTW's boundary constants; inherited infinite-state claims retain their own restrictions.
The empty volume has only the vacuum and spectral exclusion is vacuous; nonzero physical excitations are asserted for nonempty complete-factor volumes.
Fixed positive physical scales, actual onsite reference and complete interaction grouping are essential. No weak-bare-coupling continuum bridge or continuum mass-gap construction follows.
The candidate constants were shared panel proposals and the creation method is established mathematics; scientific priority remains unverified.

gate_bindings.accepted: Under the separately retained HTW smallness condition, the translated actual orthant box [-n,n]^3 and centered box [-2n,2n]^3 obey the uniform local bound min(2,exp(2C1-C2(n-2))) on the unit ball of B(H_Y), Y={0,e_z}, n>=3. The proof retains the actual whole-star boundary, all 48 links and 36 endpoints, and the domain-preserving bounded-commutator ground condition.
limitations: This loop proves a finite comparison only; diagonal finite agreement does not identify infinite-volume states.
The selected coefficient triple must be fixed and coarse-translation invariant. A changed bulk interaction is outside this comparison.
The additional HTW threshold 7|tau|<=c_HTW(1,1) and decay constants remain unevaluated; AM2 does not supply them.
Invoking the actual inherited orthant state also requires its original |tau|<tau_* restriction. Near-boundary controls show failure of this decay certificate, not actual unequal expectations.
This is a model-specific application of HTW/Yarotsky, not a continuum construction or an established priority claim.

gate_bindings.accepted: With the original orthant smallness and independent HTW condition retained, deep-bulk translates of the actual orthant state converge in local state norm to a compatible locally normal centered-box state on every fixed finite complete-factor region F. The uniform enclosure is min(2,exp(C1|F|-C2(n-r-1))) for F contained in [-r,r]^3. Independent outer cutoffs, all-pairs centered Cauchy convergence, compatibility, full gauge invariance and coarse translation invariance are established before identifying the ordered limits.
limitations: This identifies the two specified local-state routes, not their closed generators or dynamics, all possible boundary limits, or a fixed-origin boundary expectation with a bulk expectation.
Both |tau|<tau_* and 7|tau|<=c_HTW(1,1) remain; source thresholds and decay constants are positive but unevaluated.
The repeated selected coefficient triple and coarse translation convention are essential. Fine translation invariance is not asserted.
This is an application of HTW/Yarotsky under a complete boundary and domain dictionary, not a new generic theorem of boundary independence.
No physical continuum construction, mass calibration, or established literature priority follows.

gate_bindings.accepted: For the same actual origin xz Wilson and every finite whole-star orthant volume containing its complete region, the centered physical second moment obeys mu2<=alpha^2(36+28|tau|)<=alpha^2(36+7/16384)<37alpha^2. The proof derives the kinetic bound from the actual selected-strip reference, retains the exact ground scalar before its legitimate upper-bound relaxation, and proves the finite domain-valid electric commutator including its derivative cross term.
limitations: This is a finite-volume uniform moment theorem only; infinite operator-domain membership and first-moment equality require a separate limit argument.
The actual orthant state and both inherited conditions |tau|<tau_* and |tau|<=2^-16 are retained; this does not evaluate tau_*.
The two-star origin incidence cannot be substituted for an interior region or a different summable model.
Bounded second moments do not imply equality of limiting second moments. Standard commutator methods and the shared prospective panel route are acknowledged; scientific priority remains unverified.
Fixed positive physical scales and original half-Pauli normalization are essential. No continuum or experimental claim follows.

gate_bindings.accepted: For the same actual I1/AJ1/AK2 orthant physical state, chi belongs to D(H_phys), its second spectral moment is at most alpha^2(36+28|tau|)<37alpha^2, and its first moment equals alpha omega(1-W^2). Uniform first-energy tails bounded by B2/R close the former AK2 moment-loss limitation. The proof uses the actual centered spectral measures, compact spectral tests and bounded-local expectations.
limitations: Both inherited conditions |tau|<tau_* and |tau|<=2^-16 remain. This does not evaluate tau_* or identify a later numerical-cap state.
The second moment has an upper bound; equality or convergence of finite second moments is not proved, as an explicit escaping-second-moment control shows.

No common-Hilbert-space strong-resolvent or excited-vector convergence is asserted. Reverse cutoff formulas are on E>=0 and extended by zero to negative energies for C0(R) tests, as clarified in review.
The methods are established spectral and uniform-integrability arguments applied to the actual scoped Wilson state; scientific priority remains unverified.
No lowest excited energy, experimental signal, weak-coupling bridge or continuum Yang–Mills construction follows.

gate_bindings.accepted: At both signs of |tau|<=1/100000000, actual centered full-Z3 whole-star boxes have a subsequence defining a compatible locally normal gauge-invariant stationary state on the norm closure of full bounded local algebras. The actual reference reset bound is 56|tau||R|; compact-resolvent cutoffs prove local trace-norm precompactness. The matched unbounded-onsite dynamics theorem and separate local-normality argument supply strongly continuous GNS evolution with a nonnegative self-adjoint physical energy generator. The forward physical cyclic restriction is reducing; full joint-fixed completion and its positive gap remain for AQ2.
limitations: This is existence of a subsequential full-lattice state, not uniqueness of all states, whole-sequence convergence, translation invariance or all-boundary independence.
No old symbolic tau_* or HTW restriction is used, but no identity with the earlier conditional orthant or bulk state is thereby established.
Norm convergence of each local evolution as volume grows is distinct from norm continuity in time on all B(H) local operators; only the separately proved GNS strong continuity is asserted.

The compactness/dynamics/GNS/Fourier strategy is already explicit in Gauvin Supplement A.10 and uses Nachtergaele–Sims/NSY. The contribution is the reviewed SU(2) selected-strip dictionary and numerical-cap application, not invention of the generic method.
No positive physical spectral gap, Wilson operator-domain identity, calibrated mass or continuum construction is admitted by this loop.
